translation_en:
Deng Gong 鄧珙 [registered in a civilian household of Min County 閩縣, Fuzhou Prefecture 福州府, Fujian 福建; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Hongzhong 弘中; sixth in seniority among his brothers; forty-two years old, born on the first day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Deng Ziyi 子宜; his grandfather was Deng Guang 光; his father was Deng Sheng 晟; and his mother was née Lin 林氏. Both of his parents are deceased. He has an elder brother, Deng Zan 瓚, and a younger brother, Deng Ting 珽. He married née Chen 陳氏, and remarried née Lin 林氏. He placed 5th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhang 吳璋 [registered in a military household of Quanjiao County 全椒縣, Chuzhou 滁州, Directly Attached Region (Zhili 直隸); County Student (xian xuesheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Wenzan 文瓚; third in seniority among his brothers; thirty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the intercalary sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Wu Sizhong 思忠; his grandfather was Wu Jun 俊; his father is Wu Diao 釣; his mother was née Li 李氏; and his stepmother was née Du 杜氏. His father is living. He has a younger brother, Wu Huan 瓛. He married née Jin 金氏. He placed 92nd in the Yingtian Prefectural 應天府 Provincial Examination and 75th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Zhen 錢珎 [registered in an artisan household of Yuyao County 餘姚縣, Shaoxing Prefecture 紹興府, Zhejiang 浙江; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Tinggui 廷貴; first in seniority among his brothers; thirty-six years old, born on the second day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Qian Keyong 可用; his grandfather was Qian Shiming 世名; his father is Qian Shining 仕寧; his father's former wife was née Yu 余氏; and his mother is née Huang 黃氏. Both of his parents are living. He has younger brothers, Qian Xi 禧 and Qian Zuo 祚. He married née Ye 葉氏. He placed 62nd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yue 劉鉞 [registered in a civilian household of Laishui County 淶水縣, Yizhou 易州, Baoding Prefecture 保定府, Directly Attached Region (Zhili 直隸); National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Tingsu 廷肅; first in seniority among his brothers; thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Jinzhong 進忠; his grandfather is Liu Ming 名; his father is Liu Qi 琦 [Warden (siyu)]; his mother was née Chu 褚氏; and his stepmother is née Zhou 周氏. Both his grandparents and parents are living. He has younger brothers, Liu Rui 銳, Liu Yong 鏞, and Liu Hao 鎬. He married née Lu 盧氏. He placed 64th in the Shuntian Prefectural 順天府 Provincial Examination and 64th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Zan 余瓚, originally from Dantu County, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), was registered in a military household of the Wugong Central Guard. Serving as a Translator (yizi guan), he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His courtesy name was Zongzhen, he was fourth in his generation's birth order, and he was thirty sui, born on the third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu Wen, his grandfather was Yu Yuan, his father was Yu Cheng, his mother was née Du, and his stepmother was née Liu. His mother (or stepmother) was living. His elder brothers were Yu Jin, Yu Xi, and Yu Yan; his younger brothers were Yu Xuan, Yu Lian (a Translator), Yu Yu, and Yu Li. He was married to a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Ge 顏格 was registered in a civilian household of Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng), he specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His courtesy name was Zongzheng, he was second in his generation's birth order, and he was thirty-five sui, born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yan Kexie (a provincial graduate, juren), his grandfather was Yan Shichu, his father was Yan Hongchuan, and his mother was née Tu. Both of his parents were living. His elder brother was Yan Huan, and his younger brothers were Yan Gang, Yan Zhang, and Yan Pu. He was married to a woman née Shen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nan Peng 南鵬 was registered in a civilian household of Mancheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Metropolitan Area (Zhili). A County School student (xianxuesheng), he specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His courtesy name was Tengxiao, he was third in his generation's birth order, and he was twenty-eight sui, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Nan Zhong, his grandfather was Nan Zhongcheng, his father was Nan Bingyi, his legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Wang. His mother was living. His elder brothers were Nan Xiu (a Directorate student, jiansheng) and Nan Tong. He was married to a woman née Dai. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Cong 王琮 was registered in a civilian household of Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Metropolitan Area (Zhili). A Prefectural School student (fuxuesheng), he specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His courtesy name was Derun, he was first in his generation's birth order, and he was thirty sui, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Wang Jin (a Jail Warden, siyu), his grandfather was Wang Shu, his father was Wang Zhang, and his mother was née Li. Both of his parents were living. He was married to a woman née Tian. He placed fifty-first in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

羅經〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣匠籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字大常，行一，年三十三，九月十三日生〕。曾祖季新；祖彦清；父文彬；母獨孤氏。慈侍下。弟緯。娶黃氏。江西鄉試第八十九名，會試第二百九十五名。
translation_en:
Yuan Duan 袁端 (registered under a commoner household in Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; Directorate Student; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zongzheng; third in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Yuan De; his grandfather was Yuan Sheng; his father is Yuan Feng; his mother was Lady Chen, and his stepmother is Lady Li. Both his father and stepmother are living. His elder brothers are Yuan Tai and Yuan Shu, and his younger brothers are Yuan Jing and Yuan Zeng. He married Lady Yang. He placed fifty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Su 劉肅 (registered under a commoner household in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan; Subprefectural Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Jingzhi; second in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the seventh day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Liu Chaozong; his grandfather was Liu Youli; his father is Liu Xin, a Confucian Instructor; his mother is Lady Wang. Both his parents are living. His elder brother is Liu Yu, and his younger brothers are Liu Jun, Liu Mou, Liu Zhe, Liu Rui, and Liu Cheng. He married Lady Wang. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Fu 林符 (registered under a commoner household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili]; Directorate Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Chaoxin; fourth in seniority among brothers; aged thirty, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Lin Qingyin; his grandfather is Lin Guihe; his father is Lin Shiyin; his mother is Lady Xia. Both his parents and grandparents are living. His elder brothers are Lin Xiang, Lin Lin, and Lin Yong, and his younger brothers are Lin Xu, Lin Jie, and Lin Chou. He married Lady Fan. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Jing 羅經 (registered under an artisan household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi; Directorate Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Dachang; first in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Luo Jixin; his grandfather was Luo Yanqing; his father was Luo Wenbin; his mother is Lady Dugu. His mother is living. His younger brother is Luo Wei. He married Lady Huang. He placed eighty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉晟〔貫陝西鞏昌府安定縣軍籍，國子生，治《書經》，字孔昭，行一，年三十一，正月十二日生〕。曾祖文德〔元衛經歷〕；祖林〔典史〕；父武，母史氏。具慶下。弟昱。娶張氏。陝西鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百七十二名。

translation_en:
Zhang Feng 張鳳 [registered in a civilian household of Jining Subprefecture 濟寧州, Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府, Shandong 山東; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Shizhen 時禎; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-seven sui, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Wenzhong 張文中; his grandfather was Zhang Mengxiang 張孟祥; his father is Zhang Guang 張廣, and his mother is née Chen 陳氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Luan 鸞, and his younger brothers are Peng 鵬, Yuan 鵷, and Yi 鳦. He married née Zhao 趙氏. He placed sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhou 徐舟 [registered in a civilian household of Caozhou Subprefecture 曹州, Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府, Shandong 山東; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Jizhi 楫之; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty sui, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Xu Tianmin 徐天民; his grandfather was Xu Youzheng 徐友正; his father is Xu Sixue 徐思學, and his mother is née Zhang 張氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Yu 輿 and Lin 霖. He married née Yan 閻氏. He placed fortieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sheng 劉晟 [registered in a military household of Anding County 安定縣, Gongchang Prefecture 鞏昌府, Shaanxi 陝西; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Kongzhao 孔昭; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-one sui, born on the twelfth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Wende 劉文德 [Guard Registrar (wei jingli) under the Yuan dynasty]; his grandfather was Liu Lin 劉林 [District Jailor (dianshi)]; his father is Liu Wu 劉武, and his mother is née Shi 史氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Yu 昱. He married née Zhang 張氏. He placed forty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhong 劉忠 [registered in a military household of Yongfeng County 永豐縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西; National University Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Xianren 顯仁; third in seniority among his brothers; aged forty-two sui, born on the ninth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Gui'an 劉貴安; his grandfather was Liu Yunyan 劉韞彥; his father was Liu Gongchang 劉公常, and his mother was née Yuan 袁氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Duan 端 and Ren 仁, and his younger brother is Shu 恕 [Vice Director (yuanwailang) in the Ministry of Justice]. He married née Jiang 江氏. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Lin 徐霖 (native of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, of official household registration; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yongji; eighth in seniority; age twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Zhizhong; his grandfather was Mengchang; his father is Guirang; his mother is née He. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Jianxue, Fu, Shu, Zhen, Lei, and Bin, and his younger brother is Ji. He is married to née Chen. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingzhang 李廷章 (native of Shidai County, Chizhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili], of civilian household registration; a Directorate Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zichun; fourth in seniority; age thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Xingming; his grandfather was Yongzhi; his father was Shiqi; his mother was née Wang. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Ziliang, Zimao, and Ziming, and his younger brother is Guansheng. He is married to née Hu. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Mian 鄧冕 (native of Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, of civilian household registration; a County Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Chaoyi; eighth in seniority; age thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Zheng'er; his grandfather was Zhong; his father is Siwen; his mother is née Chen. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Chang and Dan. He is married to née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundred and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Xuan 乙瑄 (native of Haizhou, Huai'an Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili], of civilian household registration; a Directorate Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Chongbi; first in seniority; age thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Zhongming; his father is Wenju; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother is née Zhang. His father and stepmother are both living. His younger brothers are Lian, Zhen, and Huan. He is married to née Zhuang. He placed forty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Qing 陳清 (registered as an artisan household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; a Directorate Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Yuzhi, second in seniority, aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Chen Guanyou, his grandfather was Chen Ke'an, his father was Chen Rang, his father's former wife was Lady Shen, and his mother was Lady Ren. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Chen Cheng, and his younger brothers are Chen Wei, Chen Dan, Chen Jin, and Chen Yuan. He is married to Lady Fu. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Da 王達 (registered as a civilian household of Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; a Directorate Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Defu, second in seniority, aged twenty-seven, born on the third day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Wang Jingming, his grandfather was Wang Yongfang, his father was Wang Zirong, and his mother was Lady Zhao. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Wang Wan, and his younger brothers are Wang Mao, Wang Jiong, and Wang Dao. He is married to Lady Wu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and three hundred and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Zhen 馮鎮 (registered as a military household of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang; a Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Shiyong, ninth in seniority, aged twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Feng Mengjun, his grandfather was Feng Mo, his father was Feng Yin, and his mother was Lady Tong. His father is living. His elder brothers are Feng E and Feng Qin, and his younger brother is Feng Yi. He is married to Lady Shao. He placed sixty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bi 張賁 (a native of Luxi County, Huguang, registered as a military household of the Sichuan Escort Guard; a Student of the Huayang County School specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yanzhi, sixth in seniority, aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Zhang Xinyi, his grandfather was Zhang Congyi, his father was Zhang Hai, his mother was Lady Leng, and his stepmothers were Lady Wang and Lady Wu. His father and stepmother are living. His elder brothers are Zhang Yanying, Zhang Yanhua, Zhang Yanfang, Zhang Yanlan, and Zhang Yanzhi. He is married to Lady Chen. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

馬自然〔貫四川成都府內江縣民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字思勉，行二，年二十七，二月十二日生〕。曾祖復〔知縣〕；祖惟慶；父琳；母傅氏。具慶下，兄浩然，弟栗然、囂然、儼然、湛然、裒然。娶鍾氏。四川鄉試第七十名，會試第二百三十四名。
translation_en:
Bai Siming 白思明 [registered in a military household of Pingding Department, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi; Student of the Directorate of Imperial Academy (guozisheng); specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing); style name Ruizhi; seniority first; age twenty-five, born on the first day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Bai Xun [Princely Tribunal Judge]; his grandfather is Bai Qi [granted the title of Investigating Censor]; his father is Bai Jie; and his mother is née Shi. Both his parents and grandparents are living; his younger brothers are Sicong, Siyi, Siwen, and Sixiao. He married née Lü. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan 王璿 [registered in a civilian household of Anyue County, Tongchuan Department, Sichuan; Department Student; specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing); style name Zongshun; seniority first; age thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Fushun; his grandfather is Wang Daoxuan; his father is Wang Shouwen [District Magistrate]; and his mother is née Zhang. Both his parents and grandparents are living; his younger brothers are Ji, Yu, Heng, Pei, and Cong. He married née Gao. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zhang 唐章 [registered in a civilian household of Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili; Student of the Directorate of Imperial Academy (guozisheng); specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing); style name Zongming; seniority second; age thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Tang Boliang; his grandfather was Tang Guang; his father is Tang Hao; and his mother is née Zhou. Both his parents are living; his elder brother is Biao, and his younger brothers are Feng, Luan, and Peng. He married née Liu, and took née Duan as his second wife. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Ziran 馬自然 [registered in a civilian household of Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; Student of the Directorate of Imperial Academy (guozisheng); specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing); style name Simian; seniority second; age twenty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Ma Fu [District Magistrate]; his grandfather was Ma Weiqing; his father is Ma Lin; and his mother is née Fu. Both his parents are living; his elder brother is Haoran, and his younger brothers are Liran, Xiaoran, Yanran, Zhanran, and Pouran. He married née Zhong. He placed seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Huan 張瓛: Registered in a military salt-producer household in Taizhou 泰州, Yangzhou Prefecture 揚州府, Directly Attached Territory (Zhili 直隸); a Subprefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經); courtesy name Jingxiu 敬脩, sixth in generational order, aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xunzhi 遜之, his grandfather was Yuanshan 原善, his father is Minxue 敏學, and his mother is née Tang 唐氏. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Ying 瑛, Zhen 珎, Qi 玘, Xuan 璿, and Cheng 珵, and he married née Xu 徐氏. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefectural 應天府 Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lian 張廉: Registered in a civilian household in Yidu County 益都縣, Qingzhou Prefecture 青州府, Shandong 山東; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經); courtesy name Weijie 惟潔, second in generational order, aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xizeng 希曾, his grandfather was Mao 茂, his father is Da 達 (Vice Magistrate), and his mother is née Sun 孫氏. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Qing 慶, his younger brothers are Xu 序 and Yong 庸, and he married née Wang 王氏. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shandong 山東 Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jiong 馬駉: Registered in a military household in Xinhui County 新會縣, Guangzhou Prefecture 廣州府, Guangdong 廣東; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經); courtesy name Keyi 克毅, first in generational order, aged forty-four, born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yisun 宜孫, his grandfather was Ziwan 子晚, his father was Liang 良, and his mother was née Liang 梁氏. Both parents are deceased. His younger brothers are Hua 驊 and Xun 馴, and he married née Song 宋氏. He placed thirty-third in the Guangdong 廣東 Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xian 李顯: Registered in a civilian household in Anyang County 安陽縣, Zhangde Prefecture 彰德府, Henan 河南; a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing 書經); courtesy name Daozhang 道彰, fifth in generational order, aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhong 彥忠, his grandfather was Mao 茂 (Vice Salt Distribution Commissioner), his father was Ju 舉, and his mother is née Li 栗氏. His mother is living (father deceased). His elder brothers are Sheng 昇, Yu 昱, Min 旻, and Jing 景, and he married née Liu 劉氏. He placed seventy-third in the Henan 河南 Provincial Examination and two hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

汪洪〔貫湖廣蒲圻縣人，順天府大興縣官籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字克容，行一，年二十九，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖衡；祖秀；父勝〔順天府經歷〕；母徐氏。具慶下。弟浩。娶張氏。順天府鄉試第一名，會試第二百七十六名。

華秉彜〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣官籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字天性，行三，年二十九，五月二十七日生〕。曾祖仲和；祖子忠；父旭〔推官〕；嫡母周氏；生母吳氏。具慶下。兄寛、敏；弟秉文、秉仁、秉直、秉衡。娶沈氏。應天府鄉試第四十七名，會試第一百十四名。
translation_en:
Guo Tang 郭鏜 (registered under a military household in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong; a county student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zisheng, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Zhongbin (a Yuan-dynasty Overseer [Darughachi]), his grandfather was Zongxian (posthumously honoured as Office of Scrutiny Supervising Secretary), his father was Lin (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), his father's former wife was Madam Zhang (invested as Child Nurturer [ruren]), and his mother was Madam Li. Both of his parents are deceased. His younger brothers are Chao (a licentiate [shengyuan]), Yu, and Ben; he married Madam Liu and subsequently remarried Madam Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yu 王俁 (registered under a civilian household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Dayong, seventh in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Xinfu, his grandfather was Yancheng (posthumously honoured as Secretary in a Bureau of the Ministry of Justice), his father is Xuan (Surveillance Commissioner), his father's former wife was Madam Zhou (posthumously honoured as Pacifier [anren]), and his mother is Madam Pan (invested as Pacifier [anren]). Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Ming, Yi, Yan, and Jian; his younger brothers are Li, Xi, and Ji; and he is married to Madam Zhang. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and three hundred and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hong 汪洪 (a native of Puqi County, Huguang, registered under an official household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture; a prefectural student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Kerong, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month). His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather was Xiu, his father is Sheng (Registrar of Shuntian Prefecture), and his mother is Madam Xu. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Hao, and he is married to Madam Zhang. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and two hundred and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Bingyi 華秉彜 (registered under an official household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Tianxing, third in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Zhonghe, his grandfather was Zizhong, his father is Xu (Prefectural Judge), his legal mother is Madam Zhou, and his birth mother is Madam Wu. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Kuan and Min; his younger brothers are Bingwen, Bingren, Bingzhi, and Bingheng; and he is married to Madam Shen. He placed forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:

His great-grandfather was Yu Yanguang, his grandfather was Yu Zhoubao, his father is Yu Keli, and his mother is née Zheng. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Yu Rui; his younger brothers are Yu Shan, Yu Xi, Yu Zhen, Yu Jiu, Yu Zhang, Yu Jie, Yu Lin, and Yu Rong; and he is married to née Liu. He placed 54th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jing 李敬 [registered in a civilian household in Gaoyang County, Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili; County Student; specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Chengxue; first in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Li Juren, his grandfather was Li Gongzheng, his father is Li Duan, and his mother is née Yin. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Li Xiao, and he is married to née Zhang. He placed 39th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Yong 梁鏞 [registered in a civilian household in Gaotang Department, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong; National University Student; specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Kexuan; first in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month]. His great-grandfather was Liang Bindao [Police Chief], his grandfather was Liang Zongde [Assistant Magistrate], his father was Liang Heng, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents are deceased. His younger brothers are Liang Yue, Liang Yi, and Liang Hong, and he is married to née Chen. He placed 9th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jie 張介 [registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; National University Student; specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Lianfu; second in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Chaode, his grandfather was Zhang Huan [Prefectural Instructor of Astrology and Divination], his father was Zhang Yanli, and his mother is née Gan. His father is deceased and his mother is living. His elder brother is Zhang Xie; his younger brothers are Zhang Cui, Zhang Zhao, and Zhang Jie; and he is married to née Yin. He placed 15th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His elder brothers are Ze 澤 and Cheng 澄; his younger brothers are Jishun 吉順, Jizhen 吉禎, and Jichang 吉昌; and he is married to née Li 李氏. He placed forty-second in the Shuntian Prefectural Examination and two hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yu 李昱 [registered in a military household of Neixiang County, Dengzhou Department, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan; an added student of the county school; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Mengyang; first in seniority; aged twenty-six, born on the fifth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Li Zongyi 宗逸; his grandfather was Li Shi 實 [posthumously honored as Assistant Prefect]; his father is Li Su 素 [Vice Prefect]; and his mother is née Wang 王氏 [invested as Mistress of Peace]. Han Wen 韓文 [registered in a military household of Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; a county school student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Guandao; second in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month]. Hao Gong 郝珙 [registered as a commoner of Anyi County, Xiezhou Department, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Tingbi; second in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the third month]. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Yan 琰; his younger brothers are Fan 璠, Xu 頊, and Xuan 玹; and he is married to née Chen 陳氏. He placed twenty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張澍〔貫河南河南府新安縣，軍籍。府學生，治《詩經》。字道濟，行一，年三十七，七月二十七日生〕。曾祖時中〔府通判〕；祖宗玉〔知縣〕；父鉞〔進士、同知〕；母宰氏；繼母方氏。具慶下。弟浣、瀾、溥。娶王氏。河南鄉試第十二名，會試第三百三十八名。

陳義〔貫江西撫州府樂安縣，民籍。國子生，治《詩經》。字集義，行一，年四十，一一月十七日生〕。曾祖孟謙；祖叔賢；父懷舉；母丘氏；繼母曽氏、鄭氏。嚴侍下。弟集成、集學、集英、集彥。娶帥氏。應天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第三百三十三名。

李轍〔貫湖廣辰州府沅陵縣，軍籍。國子生，治《書經》。字由道，行二，年三十三，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖德〔元學錄〕；祖郁；父霆；嫡母曹氏；生母陳氏。慈侍下。兄軾；弟輗、軏。娶方氏。湖廣鄉試第七十五名，會試第四十三名。
translation_en:
Zhang Lian 張廉 (registered in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian household status; National University Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Mengjie, second in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Zhang Kerang 克讓; his grandfather was Zhang Zhongwen 仲文 (posthumously honoured as Surveillance Vice Commissioner); his father was Zhang Yi 翼 (Left Administration Vice Commissioner); his father's former wives were Lady Zhu 朱氏 and Lady Yang 楊氏 (both posthumously honoured as Respectful Ladies); and his mother is Lady Guan 管氏 (invested as Respectful Lady). His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brother is Zhang Kang 康. He married Lady Fei 費氏, and subsequently married Lady Zhang 章氏. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shu 張澍 (registered in Xin'an County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, under military household status; Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Daoji, first in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Zhang Shizhong 時中 (Prefectural Assistant Prefect); his grandfather was Zhang Zongyu 宗玉 (County Magistrate); his father is Zhang Yue 鉞 (metropolitan graduate (jinshi) and Vice Prefect); his mother was Lady Zai 宰氏; and his stepmother is Lady Fang 方氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Zhang Huan 浣, Zhang Lan 瀾, and Zhang Pu 溥. He married Lady Wang 王氏. He placed twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yi 陳義 (registered in Le'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, under civilian household status; National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Jiyi, first in seniority among brothers, aged forty [or forty-one], born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh [or first] month [?]). His great-grandfather was Chen Mengqian 孟謙; his grandfather was Chen Shuxian 叔賢; his father is Chen Huaiju 懷舉; his mother was Lady Qiu 丘氏; and his stepmothers were Lady Zeng 曽氏 and Lady Zheng 鄭氏. His father is living while his mother is deceased. His younger brothers are Chen Jicheng 集成, Chen Jixue 集學, Chen Jiying 集英, and Chen Jiyan 集彥. He married Lady Shuai 帥氏. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhe 李轍 (registered in Yuanling County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, under military household status; National University Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Youdao, second in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Li De 德 (Academic Director under the Yuan dynasty); his grandfather was Li Yu 郁; his father was Li Ting 霆; his legal mother was Lady Cao 曹氏; and his birth mother is Lady Chen 陳氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brother is Li Shi 軾, and his younger brothers are Li Ni 輗 and Li Yue 軏. He married Lady Fang 方氏. He placed seventy-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fang 李芳 [native of Lijin County, Bin Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, of civilian registration; National University Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Dexin, fourth in seniority, age thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Li Yanshi [invested as Secretary of a Bureau]; his grandfather was Li Yi [Left Administration Vice Commissioner]; his father was Li Cong [Instructor]; his father's first wife was née Sun; his mother was née Lang. Both parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Ying, Jin, Ying, and Zong [Assistant Instructor]; his younger brothers are Hua, Lan, Hui, Lu, and Heng. He married née Wang. He ranked 55th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhi 汪直 [native of Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili), of military registration; National University Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Maojian, first in seniority, age thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Yunshao; his grandfather was Wang Minzheng [invested as Secretary of a Bureau]; his father is Wang Huixian [Prefect]; his mother is née Jiang [invested as Mistress of Peace]. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Biao, Yue, Fan, and Meng. He married née Xie. He ranked 40th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Yan 余琰 [native of Qingshen County, Mei Subprefecture, Sichuan, of civilian registration; National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Gongpei, second in seniority, age thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Yu Chaozong; his grandfather was Yu Youzhong; his father was Yu Zhen; his mother is née Wei. His mother is living (his father having passed away). His elder brother is Zan. He married née Jin. He ranked 65th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Hui 楊徽 [native of Henei County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, of military registration; National University Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); style name Shunmei, second in seniority, age thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Yang Haoli; his grandfather was Yang Wenxiu [granted official cap and belt by grace precedent]; his father was Yang Zhixue [Instructor]; his mother was née Shi. Both parents are deceased. His elder brother is Fu; his younger brother is Lai. He married née Yan. He ranked 2nd in the Henan Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Bing 蔣昺, registered under a military household in Qiu County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji), with the courtesy name Keming, second in his generation, aged twenty-six, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jiang Da, his grandfather was Jiang Qian, his father is Jiang Yi, and his mother is Lady Li; both his parents and grandparents are living. His elder brother is Jiang Min, his younger brothers are Jiang Hao, Jiang Sheng, and Jiang Tan, and he is married to Lady Gao. He placed thirty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi 王義, registered under a military household in Luochuan County, Fuzhou, Yan'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), with the courtesy name Xunli, fourth in his generation, aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wang Mindao, his grandfather was Wang Sicheng, his father was Wang Hui, and his mother was Lady Fu; both his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Wang Zhi, Wang Quan, and Wang Yong, his younger brother is Wang Shun, and he is married to Lady Li. He placed forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Si Zhong 佀鍾, registered under a civilian household in Yuncheng County, Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an Added Student of the County School specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing), with the courtesy name Daqi, second in his generation, aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Si Defu, his grandfather was Si Boxiang, his father was Si Liangshan, and his mother is Lady Fan; his father is deceased and his mother is living. His elder brother is Si Ling, his younger brother is Si Chun, and he is married to Lady Wang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Yin 莫諲, registered under a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Directly Attached (Zhili), was a National University Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing), with the courtesy name Rujing, second in his generation, aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Mo Jingxing, his grandfather was Mo Wenyi, his father was Mo Zhong, and his mother was Lady Luo; both his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Mo Qian, and he is married to Lady Lu. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Hao 沈浩 (courtesy name Weiguang 惟廣, sixth in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month) is a native of Shangyuan County 上元縣 in Yingtian Prefecture 應天府, registered in a military household under the Embroidered-Uniform Guard 錦衣衛; he is a military student of the Shuntian Prefectural School 順天府學 specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His great-grandfather was Shen Yuancheng 沈元成, his grandfather was Shen Gui 沈貴, his father is Shen Xuan 沈瑄, and his mother is Lady Jing 景氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Shen Yan 沈儼, Shen Min 沈旻, Shen Chang 沈昌, Shen Shun 沈順, and Shen Jie 沈傑; his younger brother is Shen Xin 沈信; and he is married to Lady Pan 潘氏. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhen Xixian 甄希賢 (courtesy name Shimian 士勉, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the fifth day of the second month) is registered in a military household in Linyou County 麟遊縣, Fengxiang Prefecture 鳳翔府, Shaanxi 陝西; he is a student of the Directorate of Education (Guozisheng) specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing). His great-grandfather was Zhen Zhongde 甄仲得 (posthumously honoured as Prefectural Governor), his grandfather was Zhen Yi 甄義 (Left Vice Minister of War), his father is Zhen Qi 甄錡, and his mother is Lady Kang 康氏. Both of his parents are living, and he is married to Lady Li 李氏. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Tinggui 崔廷圭 (courtesy name Guoxin 國信, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-eight, born on the first day of the fourth month) is registered in a military household in Panyu County 番禺縣, Guangzhou Prefecture 廣州府, Guangdong 廣東; he is a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Cui Wuqing 崔武卿, his grandfather was Cui Yidi 崔義弟, his father was Cui Funu 崔福挐 [?], and his mother is Lady Lin 林氏. His father is deceased and his mother is living. His younger brothers are Cui Tingqi 崔廷器 and Cui Tingrui 崔廷瑞, and he is married to Lady Lin 林氏. He placed seventy-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and two hundred and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenzhong 李文中 (courtesy name Zongdao 宗道, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third month) is registered in a military household in Rongchang County 榮昌縣, Chongqing Prefecture 重慶府, Sichuan 四川; he is a county school student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji). His great-grandfather was Li Shiyong 李世用, his grandfather was Li Yuan 李淵 (Vice Magistrate), his father is Li Renyi 李人儀 (Prefect), and his mother is Lady Zhang 張氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Li Bianzhong 李卞中, Li Xiangzhong 李襄中, and Li Zhangzhong 李章中, and he is married to Lady Cao 曹氏. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Kui 汪奎 [native of Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), of military registration; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Wencan, fourth in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Yuan; his grandfather was Wang Lu; his father is Wang Shutai; his mother is Lady Jiang. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Wang Mengtan, Wang Mengqi, and Wang Mengkun. He married Lady Jiang. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 28th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Qi 羅玘 [originally of Ba County, Sichuan, registered under the military status of the Lin'an Guard in Yunnan; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yongcheng, second in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the ninth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Luo Tianqi; his grandfather was Luo Yong [posthumously honored as Supervising Secretary]; his father is Luo Sheng [Assistant Surveillance Commissioner]; his mother was Lady Yang [posthumously honored as Child Nurturess (ruren)]; his stepmother is Lady Zhu [enfeoffed as Child Nurturess (ruren)]. Both parents (father and stepmother) are living. His elder brother is Luo Shan; his younger brothers are Luo Xun, Luo Wei, Luo Lian, and Luo Zan. He married Lady Fan. He placed 2nd in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ding 陳鼎 [native of Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, of commoner registration; a Subprefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Meng'an, third in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Chen Ying; his grandfather was Chen Shixiang; his father is Chen Jing; his mother was Lady Du; his stepmother is Lady Zhang. Both parents (father and stepmother) are living. His elder brothers are Chen Liang and Chen Kuan; his younger brothers are Chen Nai and Chen Zi. He married Lady Wang. He placed 7th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun An 孫安 [native of Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, of commoner registration; a National University Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Mianzhi, third in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Sun Kechang; his grandfather was Sun Yuanshan; his father is Sun Wengui; his mother was Lady Jin. His father is living. His elder brothers are Sun Rang and Sun Jing. He married Lady Jia. He placed 22nd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Chun 施純 (registered in Dong'an County 東安縣, Shuntian Prefecture 順天府, under civilian household status; an added student of the county school specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Yanhou 彥厚; fifth in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Shi Wengzu 施翁祖 (Myriarch in the Yuan dynasty, posthumously honored as Minister); his grandfather was Shi Bocheng 施伯誠 (posthumously honored as Minister); his father was Shi Li 施禮 (Minister of Justice); his legal mother is née Feng 馮氏 (invested as Lady), and his birth mother is née Ma 馬氏. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Shi Lun 施綸, Shi Jin 施縉, Shi Shen 施紳 ( Councilor in the Office of Transmission), and Shi Chun 施純 [?; 紞 Shi Dan] (Preceptor). He married née Xu 許氏. He placed 99th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 90th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cong 李聰 (registered in Shunde County 順德縣, Guangzhou Prefecture 廣州府, Guangdong 廣東, under civilian household status; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Shida 士達; first in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Li Chu'an 李處安; his grandfather was Li Hebi 李和璧; his father is Li Dezhang 李德彰; and his mother is née Chen 陳氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Li Hui 李慧, Li Ping 李平, and Li Zhi 李直. He married née Huang 黃氏. He placed 19th in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 79th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Han 柯漢 (registered in Chaoyang County 潮陽縣, Chaozhou Prefecture 潮州府, Guangdong, under civilian household status; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Shizhao 時昭; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Ke Ziping 柯子平; his grandfather was Ke Kongzuo 柯孔祚; his father was Ke Keqin 柯克勤; his mother was née Yang 楊氏; and his stepmother is née Huang 黃氏. His mother is living. His elder brother is Ke He 柯河 (Directorate Student); his younger brothers are Ke Pai 柯派, Ke Jin 柯津, Ke Jun 柯濬, Ke Feng 柯逢, Ke Yu 柯雨, and Ke Qiu 柯球. He married née Xiao 蕭氏, and remarried née Zhao 趙氏. He placed 71st in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Luxun 袁魯訓 (registered in Yichun County 宜春縣, Yuanzhou Prefecture 袁州府, Jiangxi 江西, under civilian household status; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Zongdao 宗道; second in seniority among his brothers; aged forty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Yuan Shiwen 袁世聞; his grandfather was Yuan Wenshen 袁文慎; his father is Yuan Yuanheng 袁原亨; his mother was née Yi 易氏; and his stepmother is née Huang 黃氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Yuan Jingxun 袁經訓; his younger brothers are Yuan Rui 袁睿, Yuan Xuan 袁宣, and Yuan Luwen 袁魯文. He married née Li 李氏, and remarried née Chen 陳氏. He placed [?] in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and [?] in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Chun 施純 (registered in a civilian household of Dong'an County 東安縣, Shuntian Prefecture 順天府; Added Student of the county school; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Yanhou 彥厚; fifth in seniority among his brothers; age thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Shi Wengzu 翁祖 (Myriarch of the Yuan dynasty, posthumously honored as Minister); his grandfather was Shi Bocheng 伯誠 (posthumously honored as Minister); his father was Shi Li 禮 (Minister of Justice); his principal mother was Lady Feng 馮氏 (enfeoffed as Lady); and his birth mother is Lady Ma 馬氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Shi Lun 綸, Shi Jin 縉, Shi Shen 紳 (Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Office of Transmission), and Shi Dan 紞 (Medical Instructor). He married Lady Xu 許氏. He placed ninety-ninth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cong 李聰 (registered in a civilian household of Shunde County 順德縣, Guangzhou Prefecture 廣州府, Guangdong 廣東; Student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Shida 士達; first in seniority among his brothers; age twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Li Chu'an 處安; his grandfather was Li Hebi 和璧; his father is Li Dezhang 德彰; and his mother is Lady Chen 陳氏. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Li Hui 慧, Li Ping 平, and Li Zhi 直. He married Lady Huang 黃氏. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ke Han 柯漢 (registered in a civilian household of Chaoyang County 潮陽縣, Chaozhou Prefecture 潮州府, Guangdong 廣東; Student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Shizhao 時昭; fourth in seniority among his brothers; age thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Ke Ziping 子平; his grandfather was Ke Kongzuo 孔祚; his father was Ke Keqin 克勤; his mother was Lady Yang 楊氏; and his stepmother is Lady Huang 黃氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. Liu Jun 劉俊 (native of Shen Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Northern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), of commoner registration; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Junzuo, first in his generation, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month). title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟古昔帝
王之為治也其道
亦多端矣然而有
綱焉有目焉必大
綱正而萬目舉可
===
也若唐虞之治大
綱固無不正矣不
知萬目亦盡舉歟
三代之隆其法寢
備宜乎大綱正而
alt_text:

王之爲治也其道
亦多端矣然而有

綱正而萬目舉可
===

translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: We reflect that in the governance of the emperors and kings of antiquity, the ways were indeed manifold. Yet there were overarching principles (gang) and there were detailed particulars (mu); only when the great principles are rectified and the myriad particulars are upheld can governance succeed. As for the governance of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], the great principles were assuredly without fail rectified, yet We know not whether the myriad particulars were also completely upheld? In the flourishing era of the Three Dynasties, their institutions gradually became complete, so it was fitting that the great principles were rectified and…

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
萬目舉也可歷指
其實而言歟說者
謂漢大綱正唐萬
目舉宋大綱亦正
萬目未盡舉不知
===
未正者何綱未舉
者何目與已正已
舉之綱目可得而
悉言歟我
祖宗之為治也大綱無

萬目畢也可歷指
其實而言歟說者
謂漢大綱正唐萬
目畢宋大綱亦正
萬目未盡舉不知
===
未正者何綱未畢
者何目與已正已
畢之綱目可得而
悉言歟
祖宗之為治也大綱無
punctuated: 萬目舉也，可歷指其實而言歟？說者謂漢大綱正，唐萬目舉，宋大綱亦正，萬目未盡舉，不知未正者何綱，未舉者何目，與已正已舉之綱目，可得而悉言歟？我祖宗之為治也，大綱無
translation_en: … the myriad secondary details (mu) were all attended to. Can you point out the facts one by one and speak of them? Commentators say that in the Han the great guiding principles (gang) were rectified, in the Tang the myriad secondary details were attended to, and in the Song the great guiding principles were also rectified while the myriad secondary details were not entirely attended to. Yet I do not know which guiding principles were not rectified and which secondary details were not attended to, along with which guiding principles and secondary details were already rectified and attended to—can these be recounted in full? In the governance practiced by Our Imperial Ancestors, there was no great guiding principle that was not…

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
不正萬目無不舉
固無異於古昔帝
王之治矣亦可得
而詳言歟朕嗣承
大統夙夜惓惓惟
===

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
梗化之患薄海內
外熈然泰和可以
增光
祖宗可以匹休帝王果
何行而可必有其
===
要諸士子學以待
用其於古今治道
講之熟矣請明著
于篇毋泛毋略朕
將親覽焉

translation_en: …the peril of obstructing moral transformation; and that throughout the realm within and beyond the seas, there may be radiant peace and great harmony, whereby We may add luster to Our Imperial Ancestors and match the excellence of the ancient Emperors and Kings. What course of action, indeed, will make this possible? There must be an essential key to it. You gentlemen have studied while awaiting employment, and you have thoroughly discussed the ways of governance of ancient and modern times. Please set forth your views clearly in your essays, being neither vague nor perfunctory, for We shall personally inspect them.

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
臣羅倫
臣對臣聞居天下之大位必致天下之大治致天下之
大治必正天下之大本堯舜禹湯文武之位天下之大
位也堯舜禹湯文武之治天下之大治也堯舜禹湯文
武之心天下之大本也有其心然後能致其治有其治
然後能保其位心也者帝王為治之大本也能正其心
推之以為政則以正大綱而大綱無不正以舉萬目而
萬目無不舉人倫以是而明風俗以是而厚百姓以是
而富庶夷狄以是而賓服此二帝之所以帝三王之所
以王也下迨漢唐宋諸君非不有其位也但不能致其
===
治耳非不欲致其治也但不能正其心耳此漢所以止
於漢唐所以止於唐宋所以止於宋不能唐虞三代也
陛下繼
祖宗列聖之位即堯舜禹湯文武之位也承
祖宗列聖之治即堯舜禹湯文武之治也德已盛矣猶以為
未盛治已至矣猶以為未至廼萬幾之暇進臣于
廷降賜
清問首詢唐虞三代下及漢唐宋諸君欲正大綱舉萬目
明人倫厚風俗富庶百姓賓服夷狄以增光
祖宗匹休帝王臣有以知

明人倫厚風俗富庶百姓賓服夷狄以增光
□宗匹休帝王臣有以知
punctuated:
臣羅倫。
臣對：臣聞居天下之大位，必致天下之大治；致天下之大治，必正天下之大本。堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之位，天下之大位也；堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之治，天下之大治也；堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心，天下之大本也。有其心然後能致其治，有其治然後能保其位。心也者，帝王為治之大本也。能正其心，推之以為政，則以正大綱而大綱無不正，以舉萬目而萬目無不舉；人倫以是而明，風俗以是而厚，百姓以是而富庶，夷狄以是而賓服。此二帝之所以帝，三王之所以王也。下迨漢、唐、宋諸君，非不有其位也，但不能致其治耳；非不欲致其治也，但不能正其心耳。此漢所以止於漢，唐所以止於唐，宋所以止於宋，不能唐、虞、三代也。陛下繼祖宗列聖之位，即堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之位也；承祖宗列聖之治，即堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之治也。德已盛矣，猶以為未盛；治已至矣，猶以為未至。廼萬幾之暇，進臣于廷，降賜清問，首詢唐、虞、三代，下及漢、唐、宋諸君，欲正大綱、舉萬目、明人倫、厚風俗、富庶百姓、賓服夷狄，以增光祖宗、匹休帝王。臣有以知
translation_en:
Your servant Luo Lun 羅倫.
Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that he who occupies the great position of all under Heaven must bring about the great governance of all under Heaven; and he who brings about the great governance of all under Heaven must rectify the great foundation of all under Heaven. The position of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu was the great position of all under Heaven; the governance of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu was the great governance of all under Heaven; the mind-and-heart of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu was the great foundation of all under Heaven. Only when one possesses their mind-and-heart can one bring about their governance, and only when one possesses their governance can one preserve their position. The mind-and-heart is the great foundation by which emperors and kings practice governance. If a ruler can rectify his mind-and-heart and extend it into the practice of government, then when he uses it to rectify the overarching principles, none of the overarching principles will fail to be rectified; when he uses it to uphold the myriad details, none of the myriad details will fail to be upheld. Through this, human moral relations are made clear, customs are made generous, the common people are made prosperous and numerous, and the four夷 (foreign tribes) submit in allegiance. This is whereby the Two Emperors were emperors and the Three Kings were kings. Coming down to the various rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, it was not that they did not possess the position, only that they could not bring about the governance; and it was not that they did not wish to bring about the governance, only that they could not rectify their minds-and-hearts. This is why the Han remained merely the Han, the Tang remained merely the Tang, and the Song remained merely the Song, unable to match the ages of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties. Your Majesty has succeeded to the position of the Imperial Ancestors and successive sage-rulers, which is none other than the position of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu; and You have inherited the governance of the Imperial Ancestors and successive sage-rulers, which is none other than the governance of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Your virtue is alreadyflourishing, yet You still consider it not flourishing enough; Your governance has already reached the utmost, yet You still consider it not having reached the utmost. Thus, in the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, You have summoned Your servant to the court and graciously bestowed Your pure inquiry, asking first about Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and coming down to the various rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, desiring to rectify the overarching principles, uphold the myriad details, clarify human moral relations, make customs generous, make the common people prosperous and numerous, and bring the foreign tribes into submission, so as to add luster to the Imperial Ancestors and match the glory of the ancient emperors and kings. Your servant thereby knows that…

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
陛下之心即
祖宗列聖之心即堯舜禹湯文武之心也臣也竊伏草茅
誦帝王之書學帝王之道凡生靈愁苦之狀官吏貪
酷之態風俗弊壞之由古今治亂得失之故可為流
涕可為太息思欲歷數於
玉陛下以紓平生之志以解萬民之憂以上不負
朝廷作養之恩下不負聖賢垂訓之意而未能也今幸
見錄於有司得立
玉階方寸地得不披肝瀝膽髡穎涸硯而對揚
聖天子休命於萬一乎臣竊惟古昔帝王之治也其道多
===
端然有綱焉有目焉大綱不正固不可以言治然萬
目未舉亦非盡善之道也所謂大綱不過明乎人倫
厚乎風俗之類而已所謂萬目不過教養百姓賓服
四夷之類而已治莫過於唐虞也九族既睦而百姓
昭明克諧以孝而五典克從其大綱固無不正矣百
揆四岳統治于內州牧侯伯總治于外其萬目亦無
不舉焉唐虞之大綱無不正萬目無不舉如此正非
自正舉非自舉本於堯舜之一心而已使堯之心不
能克明夫峻德舜之心不能允迪夫厥德則綱無自
而正目無自而舉也治莫過乎夏商周也禹之率由

punctuated:
陛下之心，即祖宗列聖之心，即堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心也。臣也竊伏草茅，誦帝王之書，學帝王之道，凡生靈愁苦之狀、官吏貪酷之態、風俗弊壞之由、古今治亂得失之故，可為流涕、可為太息，思欲歷數於玉陛下，以紓平生之志，以解萬民之憂，以上不負朝廷作養之恩，下不負聖賢垂訓之意，而未能也。今幸見錄於有司，得立玉階方寸地，得不披肝瀝膽、髡穎涸硯，而對揚聖天子休命於萬一乎？
臣竊惟古昔帝王之治也，其道多端，然有綱焉，有目焉。大綱不正，固不可以言治；然萬目未舉，亦非盡善之道也。所謂大綱，不過明乎人倫、厚乎風俗之類而已；所謂萬目，不過教養百姓、賓服四夷之類而已。治莫過於唐、虞也，九族既睦而百姓昭明，克諧以孝而五典克從，其大綱固無不正矣；百揆、四岳統治于內，州牧、侯伯總治于外，其萬目亦無不舉焉。唐、虞之大綱無不正、萬目無不舉如此，正非自正，舉非自舉，本於堯、舜之一心而已。使堯之心不能克明夫峻德，舜之心不能允迪夫厥德，則綱無自而正，目無自而舉也。治莫過乎夏、商、周也，禹之率由
translation_en:
… that Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind of the ancestral and successive sage emperors, which is none other than the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. When your servant lived in humble obscurity among the thatched huts, reciting the books of the emperors and kings and studying the Way of the emperors and kings, with regard to all the conditions of the living people's distress and suffering, the conduct of greedy and cruel officials and subofficial functionaries, the causes of the corruption and decay of customs, and the reasons for order and disorder, success and failure, from antiquity to the present—things over which one might shed tears and heave deep sighs—I longed to enumerate them one by one beneath the jade steps of Your Majesty, so as to fulfill my lifelong ambition, relieve the sorrows of the myriad people, above not betray the court's grace in nurturing and educating me, and below not betray the intent of the sages and worthies in handing down their teachings; yet I was unable to do so. Now, having had the good fortune to be selected by the authorities and allowed to stand upon a square inch of ground at the jade steps, how could I not bare my liver and spill my gall in utter sincerity, wear my brush tip bald and drain my inkstone dry, so as to respond to and extol the Sacred Son of Heaven's gracious mandate in even one part out of ten thousand?

Your servant venture to reflect that in the governance of the emperors and kings of antiquity, although their ways were manifold, there were fundamental principles (headropes) and there were subsidiary details (meshes). If the fundamental principles are not rectified, one certainly cannot speak of good governance; yet if the myriad subsidiary details are not attended to, neither is it the Way of complete perfection. What are called the fundamental principles are nothing more than clarifying human relationships, enriching customs, and the like; what are called the myriad subsidiary details are nothing more than educating and nourishing the hundred surnames, bringing the four夷 (foreign tribes) into submission, and the like. In good governance, none surpassed Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. When the nine branches of the kin were harmonized and the hundred surnames became illustriously virtuous, and when [Shun] was able to live in harmony through filial piety so that the five cardinal duties were fully observed, their fundamental principles were certainly rectified without exception; when the General Regulator (baikui) and the Four Peaks (siyue) governed collectively within the court, and the Provincial Pastors (zhoumu) and regional lords (houbo) governed generally in the outer realms, their myriad subsidiary details were likewise attended to without exception. That the fundamental principles of Tang and Yu were rectified without exception and their myriad subsidiary details attended to without exception in such a manner was not because the principles rectified themselves, nor because the details attended to themselves; it was rooted solely in the single mind of Yao and Shun. Had the mind of Yao been unable to illustriously manifest his lofty virtue, or had the mind of Shun been unable to sincerely pursue his virtue, then the fundamental principles would have had no means by which to be rectified, and the subsidiary details would have had no means by which to be attended to. In good governance, none surpassed the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties. In Yu's following…

典常湯之肇脩人紀文王之兹迪彝教武王之重民
五教其大綱固無不正矣禹之典則貽厥子孫湯之
風愆警于有位文之九一世禄咸和萬民武之三德
八政咸正罔缺其萬目亦無不舉焉夏商周之大綱
無不正萬目無不舉如此正非自正舉非自舉本於
禹湯文武之一心而已使禹之心不能祗台德先湯
之心不能懋昭大德文之心不能緝熈敬止武之心
不能建其有極則大本不立綱無自而正目無自而
舉也唐虞蓬蒿三代丘墟帝王為治之綱目大壞極
弊於秦漢高祖起而扶持之觀其發義帝之喪戮丁
===
公之叛則君臣之義明矣從四皓之請割衽席之愛
尊禮太公大封同姓其夫婦父子兄弟之愛厚矣高
祖之垂統如此故自是而後如文帝之孝養薄后遜
位諸王如光武之痛泣其兄東海之遜讓于弟閨門
之內雖不能比隆關雎之化也而亦無聚麀之耻矣
家庭之間雖不能齊美麟趾之盛也而亦非舐犢之
愛矣惜乎賈誼請興禮樂而文帝讓以未遑仲舒請
興學校而武帝梏於私欲其視三代教民之制何如
仲舒請限田而沮於貴幸之口師丹請限田而奪於
豪勢之門其視三代養民之制何如取士雖有四科

In Yu's canons and rules bequeathed to his descendants, Tang's warnings on the faults of the customs directed at those in office, King Wen's one-ninth land tax, hereditary emoluments, and bringing universal harmony to the myriad people, and King Wu's three virtues and eight objects of government all being rectified without deficiency—none of their myriad particulars failed to be carried out. Emperor Gaozu of Han arose and upheld them. Looking at his announcing mourning for Emperor Yi and executing Ding Gong for his treason, the righteous duty between ruler and minister was made clear; in his heeding the request of the Four Hoaryheads, severing the affection of the bedchamber, honoring and showing ritual courtesy to the Grand Sire (Taigong), and grandly enfeoffing those of the same surname, his affection between husband and wife, father and son, and elder and younger brothers was generous indeed. title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
四行之目也而初非先王造士之意矣約法雖有三
章九章之格也而初非先王制刑之本矣故說者謂
漢大綱正而萬目未盡舉不其然乎炎燼既熄三國
鼎峙而是治之綱目已分五胡雲擾六朝瓜分而是
治之綱目已裂唐太宗起而維持之除隋之亂雖比
迹湯武致治之美雖庶幾成康然觀其宫人私侍脅
父臣虜則父子之恩虧矣手刃同氣親納其妃寵幸
才人基禍唐室則其兄弟夫婦之倫滅矣太宗之垂
統如此故自是而後如高宗之上烝父妾貽禍邦家
如中宗之溺愛韋后如明皇之錮寵楊妃褻瀆天倫
===
犬彘之不若其視關睢之化為何物腥穢人紀夷狄
之不如其視麟趾之化為何事然其教民也則羽林
衛士皆授孝經高麗百濟遣子入學則依稀乎先王
教化之意其養民也有田則有租有家則有調有身
則有庸則彷彿乎先王取民之制其取士也有三科
十科之制其制刑也有三覆五覆之奏其制兵也則
百人為下府千人為中府萬人為上府而制兵之意
近於古矣其考課也則四事以考其材四善以考其
行二十七最以考其政而考績之法近於古矣故說
者謂唐萬目舉而大綱未甚正不其然乎由唐而五

…and the Four Conducts, yet from the outset this was not the intent of the former kings in cultivating scholars; and although in establishing simplified laws there were the standards of the Three Articles and the Nine Chapters, from the outset this was not the fundamental principle of the former kings in instituting punishments. Therefore, commentators say that "in the Han, the overarching principles were upright, yet the myriad details were not fully carried out"—is this not indeed so?

Once the fiery embers of the Han went out, the Three Kingdoms stood like the legs of a tripod, and the overarching principles and specific details of governance were already divided; when the Five Barbarians stirred like clouds and the Six Dynasties carved up the realm like a melon, the overarching principles and specific details of governance were torn apart. Emperor Taizong of the Tang arose to uphold and sustain them. Although his elimination of the disorder of the Sui matched the footsteps of Tang and Wu, and the beauty of the governance he achieved nearly approached that of Cheng and Kang, yet if we observe how he was privately attended by his father's palace women and coerced his father into declaring himself a vassal to the northern caitiffs, then the grace between father and son was impaired; and how he slew his own brothers with his own hand, personally took his brother's consort, and doted upon the Talented Lady (cairen), laying the foundation for disaster in the Tang house, then the moral bonds between brothers and between husband and wife were extinguished. Such was the legacy passed down by Taizong. Therefore, from this time onward, there were cases such as Emperor Gaozong committing incest with his father's concubine above, bequeathing calamity to the state; such as Emperor Zhongzong doting blindly on Empress Wei; and such as Emperor Minghuang [Xuanzong] lavishing exclusive favor upon Consort Yang. Profaning the heavenly relationships, they were worse than dogs and swine—what did they regard the transformative influence of "Ospreys Cry" (Guanju) to be? Defiling human moral order with foulness, they were inferior to the barbarians—what did they regard the transformative influence of "Feet of the Unicorn" (Linzhi) to be?

Yet in their instruction of the people, the Imperial Forest (Yulin) Guard soldiers were all taught the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing), and Koguryo and Paekche sent their sons to enter the imperial academy, which faintly resembled the intent of the former kings' moral transformation through education. In their nourishing of the people, where there was land there was the land tax (zu), where there was a household there was the household levy (diao), and where there was an adult male there was the statute labor (yong), which closely resembled the former kings' system of levying from the people. In their selection of scholars, there were the systems of three categories and ten categories; in their institution of punishments, there were the memorials for three reviews and five reviews [of death sentences]; in their organization of the military, a hundred men formed a lower garrison (xiafu), a thousand men formed a middle garrison (zhongfu), and ten thousand men formed an upper garrison (shangfu), so that the intent of their military system approached that of antiquity; and in their evaluation of officials, there were the Four Matters to test their talent, the Four Merits (sishan) to test their conduct, and the Twenty-Seven Qualifications (ershiqi zui) to test their administration, so that their method of evaluating performance approached that of antiquity. title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
季治道之綱目壞亂極矣宋祖隆興削平僭叛其得
國也本於衆心之推戴原乎天命之攸歸事周后如
母愛少帝如子其待舊君之禮厚矣鼎鐺有耳雪夜
再幸其待大臣之禮厚矣灸艾分痛法堯禪舜此其
厚於兄弟之恩也從容杯酒藩鎭解柄此其厚於將
帥之恩也入朝不留來降不殺此其厚於敵國之恩
也金匱之約卒不渝盟此其厚於母子之恩也太祖
之垂統如此故繼世之君持盈守成家庭之間藹藹
如也彷彿乎太王王季之唯諾閨門之内雍雍如也
想像乎思齊太任之温恭故先儒曰本朝有超越古
===
今者五事又曰三代而下惟本朝家法最正此其大
綱之正可見也然制度頗因五代之舊不能復三代
之制語其禮也則歐陽脩盧多遜聶崇義劉温叟擅
開戶牖而禮之論屑屑是禮也果三代之禮乎惟朱
文公之家禮可以脗合乎先王之所制而當時不能
行焉語其樂也則和峴胡安定范鎭司馬公私立徑
途而樂之論紛紛是樂也果三代之樂乎語其兵也
雖有三衙四廂之制而非成周寓兵於農之意矣語
其考課也雖有六科之設而非若四善二十七最之
詳矣贓吏之法雖若嚴矣而條目未甚詳敗軍之法

punctuated: 季，治道之綱目壞亂極矣。宋祖隆興，削平僭叛。其得國也，本於衆心之推戴，原乎天命之攸歸。事周后如母，愛少帝如子，其待舊君之禮厚矣。鼎鐺有耳，雪夜再幸，其待大臣之禮厚矣。灸艾分痛，法堯禪舜，此其厚於兄弟之恩也。從容杯酒，藩鎭解柄，此其厚於將帥之恩也。入朝不留，來降不殺，此其厚於敵國之恩也。金匱之約，卒不渝盟，此其厚於母子之恩也。太祖之垂統如此，故繼世之君，持盈守成，家庭之間，藹藹如也，彷彿乎太王、王季之唯諾；閨門之内，雍雍如也，想像乎《思齊》太任之温恭。故先儒曰：「本朝有超越古今者五事。」又曰：「三代而下，惟本朝家法最正。」此其大綱之正可見也。然制度頗因五代之舊，不能復三代之制。語其禮也，則歐陽脩、盧多遜、聶崇義、劉温叟擅開戶牖，而禮之論屑屑。是禮也，果三代之禮乎？惟朱文公之《家禮》，可以脗合乎先王之所制，而當時不能行焉。語其樂也，則和峴、胡安定、范鎭、司馬公私立徑途，而樂之論紛紛。是樂也，果三代之樂乎？語其兵也，雖有三衙、四廂之制，而非成周寓兵於農之意矣。語其考課也，雖有六科之設，而非若四善、二十七最之詳矣。贓吏之法，雖若嚴矣，而條目未甚詳；敗軍之法，
translation_en: … Dynasties, the overarching principles and detailed particulars of governance fell into extreme ruin and disorder. When the founder of the Song dynasty rose to prominence, he suppressed and pacified usurpers and rebels. His acquisition of the realm was rooted in the acclamation and support of the multitude's hearts, and originated in the convergence of the Mandate of Heaven. He served the Empress of the Later Zhou as a mother and loved the Young Emperor as a son—how generous was the ritual propriety with which he treated his former sovereigns! Saying that "even tripods and pans have ears," and twice visiting on snowy nights—how generous was the ritual propriety with which he treated his great ministers! Sharing the pain of moxibustion and emulating Yao's abdication to Shun—this was his generosity in kindness toward his brothers. Over a leisurely cup of wine, the military governors relinquished their authority—this was his generosity in kindness toward his generals and commanders. Not detaining those who came to court, and not executing those who came to surrender—this was his generosity in kindness toward enemy states. The covenant of the Golden Coffer was ultimately never betrayed—this was his generosity in kindness between mother and son. Because Taizu passed down the imperial tradition in this way, the succeeding monarchs who maintained fullness and preserved the established order had an atmosphere within the family that was warm and harmonious, resembling the respectful assent of King Tai and Wang Ji; and within the inner quarters, an atmosphere that was serene and concordant, calling to mind the gentle reverence of Tairen in the ode "Stately" (Siqi). Thus, former Confucian scholars said: "Our dynasty has five things that surpass antiquity and the present." They also said: "Since the Three Dynasties, only our dynasty's family regulations have been the most upright." From this, the uprightness of its overarching principles can be seen. Yet its institutions largely followed the old practices of the Five Dynasties and could not restore the system of the Three Dynasties. Speaking of its rites: Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, Lu Duoxun 盧多遜, Nie Chongyi 聶崇義, and Liu Wensou 劉温叟 arbitrarily opened their own schools of thought, and discussions of ritual became bogged down in minutiae. Were these rites truly the rites of the Three Dynasties? Only the Family Rituals (Jiali) of Duke Wen of Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] could tally with what the former kings had instituted, yet at the time it could not be put into practice. Speaking of its music: He Xian 和峴, Hu Anding 胡安定 [Hu Yuan 胡瑗], Fan Zhen 范鎭, and Duke Sima 司馬公 [Sima Guang 司馬光] privately established their own paths, and discussions of music became confused and divergent. Was this music truly the music of the Three Dynasties? Speaking of its military: although there was the system of the Three Metropolitan Commands and the Four Sides, it did not embody the flourishing Zhou's intent of lodging soldiers among the peasantry. Speaking of its personnel evaluation: although there was the establishment of the Six Categories, it was not as detailed as the Four Virtues and Twenty-Seven Superiors [of the Tang]. As for the laws on venal officials, although they seemed strict, their articles and specifics were not very detailed; as for the laws on defeated armies, …

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
在所立矣而禁戒未甚切此其萬目未盡舉可知然
漢唐宋之治或大綱雖正而萬目未舉或萬目雖舉
而大綱不正皆由不能心堯舜禹湯文武之心故不
能致堯舜禹湯文武之治也使能正其心以立其本
則大綱之正者自能致萬目之舉萬目之舉者必本
乎大綱之正大哉正心乎其為正大綱立萬目之本
乎洪惟
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸混一區宇觀乎
大誥君臣同遊之言則雲龍之相慶魚水之相得一唐
虞之都俞吁咈也一夏商之臣鄰贊襄也觀乎申明
===
五常之條則日星之昭著雲漢之章明一唐虞之慎
典庸禮也一夏商周之建中建極也大綱豈有一之
不正乎觀其褒善之言藹乎春溫貶惡之語凜若秋
肅一唐虞三代之命德討罪也觀其大禮之制則與
天地同節大樂之作則與天地同和一唐虞三代之
制禮作樂也萬目豈有一之不舉乎我
太祖高皇帝能致堯舜禹湯文武之治如此者以其能心
堯舜禹湯文武之心也其
垂統之善如此自是
太宗文皇帝纂脩六經四書罷黜百氏雜說大明性理之

五常之條則日星之昭著雲漢之章明一唐虞之慎
典庸禮也一夏商周之建中建極也大綱豈有一之

堯舜禹湯文武之心也其
垂統之善如此自是
太宗文皇帝纂脩六經四書罷黜百氏雜說大明性理之
punctuated:
在所立矣，而禁戒未甚切。此其萬目未盡舉可知。然漢、唐、宋之治，或大綱雖正而萬目未舉，或萬目雖舉而大綱不正，皆由不能心堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心，故不能致堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之治也。使能正其心以立其本，則大綱之正者自能致萬目之舉，萬目之舉者必本乎大綱之正。大哉正心乎！其為正大綱、立萬目之本乎！
洪惟太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，混一區宇。觀乎《大誥》君臣同遊之言，則雲龍之相慶，魚水之相得，一唐、虞之都俞吁咈也，一夏、商之臣鄰贊襄也；觀乎申明五常之條，則日星之昭著，雲漢之章明，一唐、虞之慎典庸禮也，一夏、商、周之建中建極也。大綱豈有一之不正乎？觀其褒善之言，藹乎春溫；貶惡之語，凜若秋肅，一唐、虞、三代之命德討罪也。觀其大禮之制，則與天地同節；大樂之作，則與天地同和，一唐、虞、三代之制禮作樂也。萬目豈有一之不舉乎？我太祖高皇帝能致堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之治如此者，以其能心堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心也。其垂統之善如此。自是，太宗文皇帝纂脩《六經》、《四書》，罷黜百氏雜說，大明性理之
translation_en:
… had been established in various places, the prohibitions and warnings were not very stringent. From this it can be known that the myriad details of administration were not entirely attended to. Yet in the governance of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, either the great guiding principles were rectified while the myriad details were not attended to, or the myriad details were attended to while the great guiding principles were not rectified. All of this was because they could not take the minds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as their own minds, and therefore could not achieve the governance of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Had they been able to rectify their minds in order to establish the foundation, then the rectification of the great guiding principles would naturally have brought about the attendance to the myriad details, and the attendance to the myriad details would necessarily have been rooted in the rectification of the great guiding principles. How great is the rectification of the mind! Is it not indeed the foundation for rectifying the great guiding principles and establishing the myriad details?

We humbly reflect upon how the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), soared like a dragon from the Huai region and unified the realm. When we observe the words in the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) concerning ruler and ministers sharing in camaraderie, it is like clouds and the dragon rejoicing in each other, or fish and water finding mutual delight—entirely the same as the exclamations of agreement and dissent in the courts of Tang and Yu, and entirely the same as the ministers and associates assisting and aiding in the Xia and Shang! When we observe the articles clarifying the Five Constant Virtues, they are as brightly manifest as the sun and stars, and as radiantly clear as the Milky Way—entirely the same as the careful attention to canons and employment of rites in Tang and Yu, and entirely the same as the establishment of the mean and the standard of supreme perfection in the Xia, Shang, and Zhou! How could even one of the great guiding principles not be rectified? When we observe his words praising goodness, they are as mild and genial as the warmth of spring; his words censuring evil are as stern and awe-inspiring as the severity of autumn—entirely the same as the investiture of the virtuous and punishment of the guilty in Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. When we observe his institution of great rites, they share the same measure as Heaven and Earth; his creation of great music shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth—entirely the same as the institution of rites and creation of music in Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. How could even one of the myriad details not be attended to? That our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao, was able to achieve the governance of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu in such a manner was because he was able to take the minds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as his own mind. Such was the excellence of the dynastic tradition he handed down. Thereafter, the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong, the Yongle Emperor), compiled the Six Classics and the Four Books, dismissed the miscellaneous doctrines of the Hundred Schools, greatly illuminated the learning of human nature and principle…

title: 成化二年進士登科錄
text:
學制為善隂隲孝順事實弘敷彞倫之教其大綱
固無不正萬目亦無不舉也自是
仁宗昭皇帝
宣宗章皇帝
英宗睿皇帝莫不繼體守成益弘皇極之化制禮作樂大
闡文明之治其大綱固無不正而萬目亦無不舉也
我
列聖相承能繼
太祖高皇帝之治者以其能心
太祖高皇帝之心也
===
太祖高皇帝之心即堯舜禹湯文武之心也
陛下嗣承大統益弘至治朝焉而惕夕焉而厲惓惓焉惟
大綱之是正業業焉惟萬目之是舉臣有以知
陛下是心即堯舜禹湯文武之心也即
祖宗列聖之心也
陛下即位之初
親幸辟雍作興學校嘗有意於明人倫厚風俗矣而人
倫至今未甚明風俗至今未甚厚申飭有司簡練將
帥嘗有意於安百姓服夷狄矣而百姓至今未甚安
夷狄至今未甚服誠有如
